subject: math
title: E-Math trigonometry: ratios and the sine rule Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: For the 3-4-5 triangle, what is tan theta?
questions.feedback: If you picked 4/3, that is the trap: tan = adjacent / opposite. Reteach point: TOA - tan is opposite over adjacent, so for the 3-4-5 triangle tan theta = 3/4 = 0.75, with the opposite side 3 on top and the adjacent side 4 underneath.

questions.prompt: State sin theta and cos theta for the 3-4-5 triangle.
questions.feedback: Sine is opposite over hypotenuse (3/5) and cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse (4/5). Both share the hypotenuse 5 as the denominator - if either answer used 4 as the denominator, that ratio was tangent, not sine or cosine.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly reads the TOA part of the card?
questions.feedback: TOA stands for tan = opposite / adjacent. The other options mix in the hypotenuse, which never appears in the tangent ratio at all.

questions.prompt: In one or two sentences: why does the sine rule work for a triangle with no right angle when SOH CAH TOA does not?
questions.answer: The sine rule links each side with the sine of its opposite angle, so it needs no right angle - a known side and its opposite angle form a complete pair that unlocks the other sides.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the pairing: each side sits over the sine of its opposite angle. An answer that only says 'use the formula' without the side-angle pairing means the pairing idea needs reteaching first next lesson.
